title: Bounded local generators in a fixed syntomic polynomial presentation
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $S$ an $R$-algebra, $q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, $n\in\mathbb N$, and $\varphi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow S$ a surjective $R$-algebra map [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Suppose $I=\ker\varphi$ is finitely generated. Put $p=q\cap R$ and $Q=\varphi^{-1}(q)$. Assume the map $R_p\to S_q$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and the canonical prime of $\kappa(p)\otimes_R S$ corresponding to $q$ has a principal neighbourhood which is a global complete intersection over $\kappa(p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Then there are $c\in\mathbb N$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in P$ with $c\le n$, $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\subseteq I$, and $JP_Q=IP_Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. This is equality of the extended ideals in the polynomial local ring, and makes no choice of a comparison quotient or principal localization element.

proof.text: Put p=q∩R, k=κ(p), P=R[x₁,…,xₙ], I=ker φ, and Q=φ⁻¹(q). Base change the quotient P/I≅S to k, identifying the fibre with k[x]/Ibar. The fibre-spectrum correspondence identifies the prime over q and its polynomial inverse image. Transport the principal complete-intersection neighbourhood through this identification. The conormal rank theorem gives rank c=n-d with d≤n at this fibre prime. Thus c≤n.

proof.text: The images of elements of I span the fibre ideal Ibar, and hence span its conormal module and its residue-field quotient at the prime. Choose c such images forming a residue-field basis; lift them to f₁,…,f_c in I. Denominators from localization at the prime are units and can be cleared without changing the span. Nakayama applied to the finite fibre ideal shows that these fbar_i generate its localization. Let J=(f₁,…,f_c)⊆I.

proof.text: In A=P_Q the quotient A/IA identifies with S_q. The module K=IA/JA is finite because I is finitely generated. Regard the exact sequence 0→K→A/JA→S_q→0 as one over R_p. Flatness of S_q makes k⊗K→k⊗(A/JA) injective. Coefficient reduction identifies A/pA with the polynomial fibre local ring: clear the finitely many base denominators in polynomial coefficients to prove surjectivity, and use the kernel of R_p→k to identify the kernel. Thus the last two reductions are isomorphic by the local generation of Ibar proved above, so k⊗K=0, equivalently K=pK. The ideal pA lies in the maximal ideal of A. Consequently K equals the maximal ideal times K, and Nakayama for the finite A-module K (with an empty generating family) gives K=0. Therefore JA=IA, exactly the asserted equality of ideal maps.

theorem exists_bounded_local_kernel_generators
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum S) (n : ℕ) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] S)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) (hfg : (RingHom.ker φ.toRingHom).FG)
    (hflat : (Localization.localRingHom (q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R S)) q.asIdeal
      (algebraMap R S) rfl).Flat)
    (hci : ∃ h : (q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R S)).Fiber S,
      h ∉ (PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R S (q.comap (algebraMap R S))
        ⟨q, rfl⟩).asIdeal ∧
      IsGlobalCompleteIntersection (q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap R S)).ResidueField
        (Localization.Away h)) :
    ∃ (c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R),
      c ≤ n ∧ Ideal.span (Set.range f) ≤ RingHom.ker φ.toRingHom ∧
      Ideal.map (algebraMap _
        (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.comap φ.toRingHom))) (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) =
      Ideal.map (algebraMap _
        (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.comap φ.toRingHom))) (RingHom.ker φ.toRingHom)
